paraphrase: In the beginning there was neither being nor non-being; from the unborn arose darkness, elements, the egg and the Person with a thousand heads; from him all creatures.

checks.note: E-text chapter (adhyāya, khaṇḍa or section) 1-2 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'tadāhuḥ kiṃ tadāsīttasmai sa hovāca na sannāsanna sadasaditi tasmātta-maḥ sañjāyate tamaso…').

paraphrase: The knower lives like a child, unattached, like one mute or mad.

checks.note: E-text chapter (adhyāya, khaṇḍa or section) 13 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'bālyena tiṣṭhāsedbālasvabhāvo'saṅgo niravadyo maunena pāṇḍityena niravadhi-kāratayopalabhyeta kaivalyamuktaṃ…').

paraphrase: This teaching is not to be given to one who is not calm, not a son or disciple.

checks.note: E-text chapter (adhyāya, khaṇḍa or section) 16 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'saubālabījabrahmopaniṣannāpraśāntāya dātavyā nāputrāya nāśiṣyāya nāsaṃ-vatsararātroṣitāya…').

paraphrase: He whose body is the earth, who moves within the earth and whom the earth does not know… whose body is the mind, the self… he is the inner self of all beings, free of evil, the divine, the one Nārāyaṇa.

checks.note: E-text chapter (adhyāya, khaṇḍa or section) 7 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'antaḥśarīre nihito guhāyāmaja eko nityo yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥpṛthivīmantare sañcaran yaṃ pṛthivī na veda…').
